book_xii_canal.label: BOOK XII
book_xii_canal.title: The Canal That Could Not Be Sold

canal_p01_001.speaker: narrator
canal_p01_001.text: The canal appeared beneath a line of willows that had already begun to yellow. Yue expected a broad waterway after the valley's disputes over cups and gauges. Instead she found a channel narrow enough for two people to argue across, with a flat-bottomed grain boat wedged against one bank. Its owner was asleep beneath an upturned basket. On the towpath, a woman in an indigo coat examined a lock beam while three geese disputed her place beside it.

canal_p01_002.speaker: narrator
canal_p01_002.text: Yue waited until the woman lowered her measuring stick. 'Luo Zhen?' she asked. The keeper nodded without releasing the beam. Yue offered Elder Yun's introduction, folded inside her ordinary travel cover. Luo told her to hold the geese back while she read it. The task required a broom, not cultivation. One goose defeated the first sweep and reached the keeper's boots. Luo laughed once, freed the bird's foot from a loose string and gave Yue a better angle.

canal_p01_003.speaker: narrator
canal_p01_003.text: The introduction described Yue's earned second pair and her limited experience with material paths. Luo read that line twice, then examined her hands. 'I need somebody who can tell a swollen gate from a curse,' she said. 'I can tell one from the other myself, but the council has stopped listening to me.' Behind her, the grain boat rocked free when its owner finally woke. The ordinary beam lifted a finger's width, and water sighed through the gap.

canal_p01_004.speaker: narrator
canal_p01_004.text: A public notice hung on the toll-house door. It offered the canal bed, both banks, the seasonal water right and the service obligations of twenty-eight households as one sale lot. Han Shou's seal appeared beneath the price line. The auction would occur eight weeks hence if no valid objection was received. Yue had seen lists turn people into absent names. Here the names were present, neatly written beside things somebody believed could be purchased with them.

canal_p01_005.speaker: narrator
canal_p01_005.text: Han Shou arrived before Yue finished reading. He wore a clean brown coat whose cuffs had been turned rather than replaced. He asked whether she had come to bid. When Luo called her an apprentice, he smiled with professional patience. 'Then read the whole notice before condemning it,' he said. 'The canal owes money. People enjoy common water until a gate breaks, and then they remember that timber grows in a forest somebody else has to pay to reach.'

canal_p01_006.speaker: narrator
canal_p01_006.text: Tian Min stood behind him carrying a basket of linen. She was twenty-three, Luo told Yue later, and had inherited neither a house nor a shop. Nevertheless the notice assigned six annual workdays to her father's household and named her among its successors. Tian set the linen on the dry sill and asked Han whether a bidder could command her while she was stitching somebody else's sail. He answered that the obligation belonged to the household. She asked where, exactly, a household kept its hands.

canal_p01_007.speaker: narrator
canal_p01_007.text: A toll boat brought Mo Ran with roots for the orchard. He recognized Yue at the sale notice and asked about her earlier orchard arrangement. She told him its actual duties still stood: any personal return owed remained unfulfilled, and the requested new date awaited the matron's reply. Eight days on the road had not completed a visit. Mo Ran read the household clause and became quiet. 'An old promise can have a very young back,' he said. Then he carried his roots into the shade.

canal_p01_008.speaker: narrator
canal_p01_008.text: Luo introduced Yue to the keeper's shed, a carpenter's bench and a room above the flour store where an apprentice could sleep. The lock inspection was an eight-week paid commission, funded from the canal's regular maintenance reserve and defined before the auction date. Yue would copy measurements, assist ordinary tests and perform only supervised permitted control tasks. The council also needed a property review. Luo said nobody expected Yue to turn her cultivation cord into a qualification she did not possess.

canal_p01_009.speaker: narrator
canal_p01_009.text: The first defect was a child's wooden whistle caught beneath a floating gate shoe. Its owner watched from the bank, pale with the fear of being blamed for the stalled grain boat. Luo closed the upstream hand gate and showed Yue where the ordinary flow indicator settled. Only then did she use a hooked pole to lift the whistle free. The lock moved again. Yue gave it back with its split mouthpiece visible, refusing the child's first insistence that a beast had swallowed it.

canal_p01_010.speaker: narrator
canal_p01_010.text: The child tried to blow the whistle and produced a wet squeak. His grandfather told him that every delay meant another toll, though this canal charged by the scheduled cargo turn rather than each minute. Luo corrected the claim without raising her voice. The grandfather looked toward Han, who was still talking to the boat owner about timber credit. An inaccurate toll story had traveled farther than the posted tariff. Yue copied the actual rule into the first page of her new work notebook.

canal_p01_011.speaker: narrator
canal_p01_011.text: At the flour-store stairs, Yue caught her sleeve on a nail and tugged too hard. Pain crossed her forearm, ordinary and immediate. She stopped, freed the cloth with her other hand and inspected the shallow scratch before deciding whether it changed any later task. The fourth-stage cord lay against the torn sleeve. Two opened pairs did not make every movement wise. Luo brought clean water and said the exposed nail belonged on the repair list alongside much grander problems.

canal_p01_012.speaker: narrator
canal_p01_012.text: They ate millet, pickled greens and a bowl of fish broth at the keeper's bench. Tian arrived with thread still attached to one finger and argued that the household clause made her owe work before she had earned the right to vote at the canal meeting. Han said her family had benefited from the original loan. Luo asked him how much of it remained. He answered eighty copper. Yue put down her spoon. At last there was a number small enough to follow.

canal_p01_013.speaker: narrator
canal_p01_013.text: The canal reserve held one hundred twenty copper according to the last signed count. Ninety-six had already been set aside for the season's gate and bank repairs, leaving twenty-four available for debt service. Han said the remaining eighty on the old loan justified selling the canal. Luo said the loan had assigned a share of tolls, not title to the bed. Both pointed to the same faded register. Yue could see at once why a simple sum would not settle the thing being sold.

canal_p01_014.speaker: narrator
canal_p01_014.text: The original advance had paid for timber after a flood, twenty-four years earlier. Some of the people named on its first page were dead. Others remembered their parents returning from the bank with split nails and mud inside their sleeves. Tian's father had become ill that winter and died years later. She disliked hearing the loan described as a gift to his descendants. Han disliked hearing it described as if his mother's lent copper had become worthless because time passed.

canal_p01_015.speaker: narrator
canal_p01_015.text: 'My mother went hungry to buy those beams,' Han said. Tian asked whether his hunger could become her six days every year. He started to answer about gratitude, then stopped. Yue watched his eyes move between the loan number and the household names. His claim had a real beginning. The notice had enlarged that beginning into a much wider present. She would have to understand both if the review was to change anything beyond who spoke most confidently at supper.

canal_p01_016.speaker: narrator
canal_p01_016.text: After the meal, Luo took Yue along the left bank. Reed roots held one reach together; fresh footprints weakened another. Three houses opened directly onto the towpath, with drying racks placed high enough for a rope team to pass beneath. A woman called to Luo about the leaking lower gate, then lowered a sleeve to hide a burn on her wrist. The canal was a workplace, a road and the front yard of people's homes. Selling it as a single lot made those different uses seem strangely uniform.

canal_p01_017.speaker: narrator
canal_p01_017.text: The north private wharf stood behind a separate low wall. Han owned its storage shed, loading crane and two movable platforms. His workers were replacing a rotten board without waiting for the public council. Yue had expected the entire reach to be common property after reading the notice. Luo corrected her. The canal bed was one question; the shed and crane another. If the review confiscated genuine private goods to make a satisfying public victory, it would begin with another mistake.

canal_p01_018.speaker: narrator
canal_p01_018.text: At the far gate, Bao Jun measured the timber with a carpenter's square. He was thirty-one, broad in the shoulders and careful about where he rested his thumb. A saw accident had taught him to support a board before arguing over its cut. He showed Yue a hollow beneath the lower seal, then let her find the corresponding wear mark herself. The water escaped along a material gap. Neither the old loan nor the new auction notice had caused that particular leak.

canal_p01_019.speaker: narrator
canal_p01_019.text: Bao had ordered two replacement lengths, seals and nails under the existing repair allowance. He would not fit them until the ordinary work crew was confirmed. Han offered men from the wharf in exchange for acknowledging the household obligation. Bao refused the condition but admitted the deadline troubled him. A broken lower gate would waste water while the council debated ownership. Yue wrote the repair's physical sequence beside its staffing problem, resisting the temptation to let either explain away the other.

canal_p01_020.speaker: narrator
canal_p01_020.text: In the sleeping room, Yue unpacked her personal clothes, tablet and food bag. The objects belonged to her; none was an unreturned tool from the valley. She had left that commission's records and apparatus with their actual keepers. From the window she could see Tian sewing beneath a lamp at her door. The notice had assigned Tian's time as if it sat ready in a cupboard. Yue opened the household register copy Luo had given her and began with the first name.

canal_p01_021.speaker: narrator
canal_p01_021.text: On the second morning, the council offered three initial lines of inquiry. Yue could walk the household towpath with Tian, compare the boundary marks with Luo, or hear Han's surviving loan history before the archive opened. The clerk would gather the other records in parallel. No first conversation could decide the auction's validity. Yue chose which relationship she wanted to understand before the documents began telling her what everyone ought to have done.

choices.text: Walk the household towpath with Tian Min.
Compare the boundary marks with Luo Zhen.
Hear Han Shou's surviving loan history.

canal_p01_022.speaker: narrator
canal_p01_022.text: Tian began at a house whose door lintel leaned toward the water. Her aunt lived there with two grandchildren and a loom repaired so many times that no original peg remained. The auction notice assigned the household six workdays, but its entry still named Tian's grandfather as available labor. He had died eleven years earlier. The aunt did not want her family's history erased. She wanted someone to explain why remembering him entitled a buyer to command the children at his table.

canal_p01_023.speaker: narrator
canal_p01_023.text: The younger grandchild offered to work all six days if the buyer fixed their roof. Tian told him the offer was generous and impossible to judge without a task or price. Yue asked what he already did during harvest. He listed carrying grain, gathering reeds and watching his sister after school. There was no empty child in the house waiting to become useful. The register's tidy obligation had concealed a calendar already full of necessary work.

canal_p01_024.speaker: narrator
canal_p01_024.text: At the next gate, a sailmaker defended the old duty. His family had completed its share proudly, and he thought Tian's objections dishonored them. Tian put down her basket before answering. 'Then let their completed work count,' she said. 'Don't keep making us perform it again to prove they meant it.' The sailmaker's face changed. He took a wrapped bundle from his beam shelf and showed them a toll-house acknowledgment his mother had kept beside her finest needles.

canal_p01_025.speaker: narrator
canal_p01_025.text: The acknowledgment recorded twelve completed days across two seasons, with a smaller note about the following year's flood interruption. Yue copied its number and folded-corner marks. It could support the family's account without settling the whole pledge. The sailmaker asked her to call it a release. She said the original terms would determine that. Tian looked irritated by the restraint. Outside, she admitted she wanted the first useful paper to free everyone immediately, because waiting had already used so much of their lives.

canal_p01_026.speaker: narrator
canal_p01_026.text: One household had rented its towpath room from Han and supported his sale plan. Its head hoped a private owner would repair the drain more quickly than the council. Tian argued, then caught herself speaking as if he had betrayed the whole bank. Yue asked what the drain had done last winter. He showed a waterline above his sleeping platform. The ownership proposal offered him a concrete improvement. Any common plan would need to address that waterline, not merely correct his politics.

canal_p01_027.speaker: narrator
canal_p01_027.text: They measured the drain from the dry bank, finding silt beneath a narrow crossing plank. Luo's repair list included it, but the council had postponed clearing because a private platform covered the working edge. Han's wharf and the common drain met there physically. A future agreement would need access under the platform without claiming the platform itself. Tian drew the crossing on Yue's slate and said this was the first part of the sale notice that had looked like a practical question.

canal_p01_028.speaker: narrator
canal_p01_028.text: Near the reed beds, two households were absent on seasonal work. Their doors were tied, their grain jars stored with neighbors and their six-day entries marked 'successors available.' No successor lived there. Tian had been asked to produce relatives from another village. She said she could send them the notice, but would not sign on their behalf. Yue recorded the actual absence and asked the clerk to preserve a means of reply that did not require returning before the eight-week auction date.

canal_p01_029.speaker: narrator
canal_p01_029.text: By noon, the walk had shown a bank with different hopes rather than twenty-eight interchangeable opponents. Some wanted release from a duty, some wanted recognition of work completed, some wanted a repaired drain badly enough to welcome a buyer. Yue returned with receipt numbers and ordinary repair locations. Tian returned with a harder task: represent households without pretending all of them wanted the same remedy. They stopped at her door to fold the linen before the afternoon rain touched it.

canal_p01_030.speaker: narrator
canal_p01_030.text: Luo took Yue to a boundary stone half buried beneath willow roots. Its old carving divided the watercourse from the loading plot, but a newer white line crossed both. Han's workers had painted that line while measuring the proposed sale lot. Paint could guide a survey without becoming title. Yue brushed away loose leaves with a dry branch while Luo read the surviving stone marks. The stone's weathered authority also had limits: it could show a boundary description, not the current rights of every user.

canal_p01_031.speaker: narrator
canal_p01_031.text: Farther north, a second stone had tipped into the water after bank erosion. They left it untouched while Luo checked its recorded location against an old measured plan. Pulling it upright might improve its appearance while destroying evidence of the movement. Bao arrived with a rope and was ready to help, but Luo stopped him. He understood as soon as she showed the plan. The canal needed a survey before a repair changed the landmarks the survey was supposed to compare.

canal_p01_032.speaker: narrator
canal_p01_032.text: A wharf worker challenged them at the wall, believing Yue had come to seize the crane. Luo explained the two questions separately: determine the canal boundary and record Han's private structures. The worker relaxed enough to show where the crane foot had been rebuilt. Its base stayed inside the loading plot, though its swinging beam crossed the public towpath during lifts. Ownership of a crane did not automatically grant uninterrupted use of every space its beam could reach.

canal_p01_033.speaker: narrator
canal_p01_033.text: Yue watched a load of salt sacks pass beneath the beam. The worker blocked the towpath with an ordinary red board until the lift settled. That practice protected walkers, but the closure had no agreed maximum interval. A schoolgirl waited nearly half an hour with a lunch bowl. She cared little about the deed. She wanted a way to get home before her soup cooled. Luo recorded the interval beside the crane's swing diagram, giving a small obstruction the same careful attention as the disputed sale.

canal_p01_034.speaker: narrator
canal_p01_034.text: The old plan marked a flood spill beyond the north plot. Han's notice included it within the lot, calling it unused waste ground. At low water it did look like a reed-filled hollow. Luo showed Yue a line of deposited twigs caught above knee height. Previous floods had used the hollow. Its function could disappear from view without ending. Yue sketched the high marks and requested the keeper's older flood observations rather than letting this season's dry reeds define what the ground could do.

canal_p01_035.speaker: narrator
canal_p01_035.text: Han joined them at the spill and said he intended to fill it for storage. Luo asked where the next high flow would go. He pointed downstream, then hesitated when she placed the old plan beneath his hand. The marked diversion would lose its entrance. He said a stronger lower bank might compensate. That was a proposal requiring dimensions, material and flow checks, not a fact earned by confidence. Yue wrote it as a proposed replacement, with the missing assessment left visible.

canal_p01_036.speaker: narrator
canal_p01_036.text: At the returning bend, Luo admitted she had once approved a temporary platform over the spill's edge. It had remained three seasons longer than intended. The keeper's own concession had helped make the hollow look disposable. Yue asked why she had allowed it. A bad harvest had left the wharf desperate for dry space, and the council promised a later review. The later review never came. Luo kept walking after the admission, neither excusing it nor inviting Yue to pretend it had not mattered.

canal_p01_037.speaker: narrator
canal_p01_037.text: Back at the shed, they placed the boundary plan beside the actual-use map. Public waterbed, private loading plot, swinging crane, common path and seasonal spill did not fit into one bright outline. The sale notice had made them a single lot because a single lot was easier to price. Yue's map grew less beautiful as it grew more accurate. Luo said an ugly useful map might keep them from replacing one simple story with another equally expensive one.

canal_p01_038.speaker: narrator
canal_p01_038.text: Han received Yue in the north shed, where the walls smelled of dry cedar. A framed tally hung above his desk. It named his mother's original timber advance and the first flood season's deliveries. He said people called her rich now because they could see the shed, forgetting the years when it was an open platform and a chest of unpaid accounts. Yue asked him to begin with the advance itself, before the pride and resentment surrounding it turned its terms into something else.

canal_p01_039.speaker: narrator
canal_p01_039.text: The original sum was two hundred forty copper. Han's mother supplied timber through two local cutters and a boat crew, with the canal council accepting repayment from a specified toll share. A labor annex accompanied the agreement, he said, but his working copy described its duration poorly. He had assumed household duties continued while any cash remained unpaid. Yue asked to see the wording that made those different obligations depend on one another. Han opened a drawer and took out a transcription rather than the original.

canal_p01_040.speaker: narrator
canal_p01_040.text: The transcription read 'sixty maintenance days, renewed in season.' Its heading contained no number of seasons. Beneath it, a later hand had added household successor names. Han said he had followed the copy used by his father. Yue asked when the copy was made. He could not remember. A practice handed down through two owners might explain why he trusted it; it did not establish that the copied heading preserved the original duration. He agreed to let the clerk compare it.

canal_p01_041.speaker: narrator
canal_p01_041.text: Han's wife brought tea and left without joining the conversation. He waited until the door closed before saying the wharf had a loan of its own, due after the autumn trade. Selling a canal lot would clear it. That pressure made the proposed auction understandable without making the property his. Yue asked whether the buyer had already offered money. He admitted taking a conditional deposit. The buyer expected the household services as part of the value, and might demand repayment if the title failed.

canal_p01_042.speaker: narrator
canal_p01_042.text: The deposit was secured against Han's private loading gear, according to the agreement he showed her. It was not a new charge on the common canal reserve. Yue copied the distinction carefully. Han seemed relieved that she had noticed it, then angry that relief looked like retreat. He asked whether common ownership meant merchants must bear every cost while households kept every benefit. Yue said she had come to find the actual costs and obligations, because that question could not be answered fairly in its broadest form.

canal_p01_043.speaker: narrator
canal_p01_043.text: On the shed wall, Han showed a mark where the founding flood had reached his mother's shoulder. He remembered her carrying a ledger above the water while his father supported his injured leg. The memory made him speak softly for the first time. Yue remembered her own mother lifting flour from a wet shelf and understood his loyalty. She still asked whether preserving that ledger required treating Tian's hours as part of its furniture. Han looked at the water mark and did not answer.

canal_p01_044.speaker: narrator
canal_p01_044.text: He did show Yue three repayment receipts totaling one hundred sixty copper. The remaining eighty was therefore a real account balance if the receipts and original terms matched. He had not invented the loan to support the auction. The uncertainty lay in what the balance entitled him to do. Yue thanked him for the copies and asked the clerk to request the original register. Han said he would come to the review, provided the council recorded his valid claim before announcing any triumph.

canal_p01_045.speaker: narrator
canal_p01_045.text: Outside, Yue found Mo Ran waiting with a root sack repaired in coarse thread. He asked whether Han was a monster. She said he was a man with a real debt, a pressured business and a notice that claimed too much. Mo Ran considered that a troublesome answer. 'Monsters sometimes make the paperwork easier,' he said. Yue laughed despite herself. Then she went back to the keeper's shed, where a canal gate still leaked regardless of how complicated its creditor had become.

canal_p01_046.speaker: narrator
canal_p01_046.text: At the archive counter, the clerk laid the morning's copied observations in three separate trays. Tian's receipt numbers, Luo's boundary map and Han's loan history were all present, gathered by the people assigned while Yue followed her chosen first inquiry. The papers disagreed in useful ways. No tray could tell them what the original labor annex said. The clerk requested it from the sealed canal register and gave Han a witnessed copy of the request before anybody accused him of withholding it.

canal_p01_047.speaker: narrator
canal_p01_047.text: Pei Fen, the retired toll clerk, arrived carrying a bowl of steamed chestnuts. She was sixty-seven and had stopped copying small columns when her eyes began turning two strokes into three. She still remembered how the old books were arranged. Han greeted her politely until she said the labor annex had once had a clear end date. He asked why she had not objected earlier. She looked at the chestnuts. 'I thought everyone could still read what I remembered.'

canal_p01_048.speaker: narrator
canal_p01_048.text: Her memory would guide a search, not replace the missing page. Pei accepted that distinction and told the clerk which spine had been repaired after the founding flood. The repair stitch used blue thread because white thread had gone to a sailmaker that week. Bao said blue thread could survive from a later repair too. Pei nodded. The detail narrowed the bundle to inspect. It could not date the annex merely by sounding precise, and she refused to sign a statement claiming it could.

canal_p01_049.speaker: narrator
canal_p01_049.text: The working transcription in Han's desk named sixty maintenance days 'renewed in season.' The public household list converted that into six days for each current family, with successors added as births and deaths changed the bank. Twenty-eight households at six days would create one hundred sixty-eight days each year, nearly three times the original annual number even if renewal had been unlimited. Yue wrote both calculations on the slate. Han studied the smaller one before arguing about the larger obligation.

canal_p01_050.speaker: narrator
canal_p01_050.text: The council chair admitted that later lists had grown through convenience. New households joined the maintenance rota; the clerk copied the full list when a wharf creditor requested names. A cooperative work list became attached to a debt description, then began to look inherited. Tian asked who first made that attachment. The clerk would search, but the current duty could be challenged without identifying one original hand. The notice now offered more work than even Han's own transcription described.

canal_p01_051.speaker: narrator
canal_p01_051.text: Han proposed reducing the annual duty to sixty days and proceeding with the sale. Luo asked him to identify the clause granting title to the canal bed. He pointed to the debt assignment. Its wording transferred the specified toll share and listed movable security, not the watercourse. The chair suspended the auction notice for comparison, retaining its eight-week review date. The suspension protected time to examine the claim. It did not decide whether eighty copper remained due or whether the private shed could be sold.

canal_p01_052.speaker: narrator
canal_p01_052.text: The clerk counted the canal chest with Han and two household witnesses present. One hundred twenty copper matched the previous signed balance. Ninety-six stayed marked for necessary gate and bank work; twenty-four could be considered for the valid loan once its payment terms were checked. Yue counted one pile again after dropping a coin beneath the stool. The delay irritated Han. She retrieved the coin before signing anything, preferring a tedious accurate balance to an elegant number nobody had actually handled.

canal_p01_053.speaker: narrator
canal_p01_053.text: The ninety-six-copper work order separated fifty-six for twenty-eight ordinary worker-days, twenty-eight for timber, seals and nails, and twelve for six charged apparatus stones. Each stone came with its own measured starting charge. Yue's scheduled twelve ordinary workdays would earn twenty-four copper within the labor line; other workers shared the remaining sixteen days. The eight-week term gave room for rain, recovery and archive replies. It did not purchase every hour of her life until the notice came down.

canal_p01_054.speaker: narrator
canal_p01_054.text: Yue read the work order in the flour-store room and marked the dates she already knew she could work. Luo had included lodging in the unused apprentice room and allowed her to cook at the keeper's hearth. Food came from Yue's own wages and ordinary provisions, not the contested loan chest. She had enough travel money for a return if the review stopped. Knowing that made it easier to say she would inspect the lower gate rather than promising to save an entire canal.

canal_p01_055.speaker: narrator
canal_p01_055.text: Jiang Tao reached the landing that evening with a short appointment to review the relay fittings. Luo had requested her before inviting Yue, because the keeper wanted a qualified apparatus operator rather than an apprentice standing in for one. Jiang's paid operating days belonged among the work order's other scheduled days. She examined the six stones without opening their sleeves. Their charge would feed rated frames during tests and protective withdrawals. It would not flow through Yue merely because she knew the trigger paths.

canal_p01_056.speaker: narrator
canal_p01_056.text: At the practice bench, Jiang asked Yue which route she wanted to use first. Yue wanted to demonstrate the second pair, then caught the eagerness in her own answer. Travel strain had made her hands stiff. They began with an ordinary sensation check and postponed qi work until the next recovered morning. Jiang did not turn the postponement into a lecture. She needed time to inspect the bench ground as well, and sent Yue to buy onions before the market closed.

canal_p01_057.speaker: narrator
canal_p01_057.text: Tian joined her at the onion stall and said she envied being able to postpone an expected performance. Her customers wanted sails ready regardless of her father's entry in the household list. Yue could not solve that with a cultivation rule. She carried the onion bag while Tian described a buyer who had demanded six unpaid repair hours because the canal supposedly owed him service. The current sale notice had already begun changing bargains outside the lock. Waiting for the auction was not a harmless interval.

canal_p01_058.speaker: narrator
canal_p01_058.text: They found the buyer beside his boat, rolling a patched sail. He said Han had never told him to claim free stitching; he had understood the household clause himself. Tian showed her paid stitch tally and refused another patch on those terms. The buyer grumbled, then agreed to the ordinary price because he needed the sail before dawn. Yue watched Tian's hands settle after the conversation. A public correction might make the next argument shorter, but this one had cost her courage now.

canal_p01_059.speaker: narrator
canal_p01_059.text: Luo wrote an interim notice stating that no buyer had acquired household labor and no new canal title had been transferred. The council chair signed it, and Han agreed to post it beside his auction paper while the claim was examined. He insisted the notice also preserve his asserted eighty-copper balance. The clerk included that as a disputed security question with a documented remaining sum. Correcting one overreach did not require printing a false statement that the original lender had been paid in full.

canal_p01_060.speaker: narrator
canal_p01_060.text: At supper, Bao asked whether the gate timber could be ordered while ownership remained disputed. The ninety-six-copper reserve had been approved for repair before the auction notice, and its custodian remained the canal council. The chair confirmed the existing order in writing. Bao would buy the two lengths, seals and nails against the twenty-eight-copper material line. He placed the order where Han could read it. Useful transparency sometimes consisted of letting an opponent inspect a purchase he could not veto.

canal_p01_061.speaker: narrator
canal_p01_061.text: The lower gate's defect kept worsening at the warmest hour. Luo's daily measurements showed that swollen timber bound against one side, then leaked through the hollow seal below. Jiang proposed an isolated model to compare the mechanical travel with the relay's stop timing. Bao proposed first fitting a straight guide to remove the binding. Neither asked Yue to force water through a blocked channel. They agreed on an ordinary inspection before a powered comparison, because the machine could not repair the wood by making a brighter signal.

canal_p01_062.speaker: narrator
canal_p01_062.text: Yue slept badly that night. She dreamed a canal running through her forearms, every household door opening from it. In the dream, she could lift the whole waterway if she admitted one more route. Waking, she felt only the familiar stiffness from travel. She wrote the dream on a private page and left the practice sheet empty. The urge to become indispensable had changed its scenery. Its promise remained the same: one unearned power would spare her the trouble of choosing a smaller honest task.

canal_p01_063.speaker: narrator
canal_p01_063.text: Mo Ran found her washing the onion pot before sunrise. He asked whether the dream had been pleasant. She said it had been useful until she woke. He told her he still dreamed of correcting Azure Cloud in a single sentence, although actual repairs kept requiring people he had once dismissed. They scrubbed a scorched patch without discussing whose dream was wiser. The pot became clean through water, ash and patience. Yue liked being able to finish something without assigning it a meaning first.

canal_p01_064.speaker: narrator
canal_p01_064.text: The morning hand check was ordinary. Jiang allowed one first-pair quarter-unit command on the isolated practice wick, within Yue's half-unit delivery allowance, followed by full discharge. The second pair remained quiet that day. The reading matched her recovered baseline. A familiar result after an unfamiliar journey reassured her more than she expected. She had brought her earned body to a new task, not started again as a novice and not advanced merely because the canal's problem looked larger.

canal_p01_065.speaker: narrator
canal_p01_065.text: At the lock, Luo let a boat through while Bao marked the swollen guide. The owner complained about the delay, then offered to help once he saw the marked fault. Luo gave him an ordinary task moving dry planks from the path. His offer was specific and finished before his departure. Yue compared it with the sale notice's endless successor line. People could contribute willingly to common work without making that contribution an asset to be sold after they left.

canal_p01_066.speaker: narrator
canal_p01_066.text: Han's buyer arrived at noon in a narrow covered boat. He was a grain dealer from upriver and had inspected only the notice, not the canal itself. The buyer asked where the storage ground began. Luo showed him the seasonal spill, still full of dry reeds. Han repeated his proposal to fill it. The buyer asked for the replacement flood assessment before confirming the offer. Commercial caution did what moral argument had not: it made the missing dimensions expensive to ignore.

canal_p01_067.speaker: narrator
canal_p01_067.text: The conditional deposit remained secured against Han's loading gear. The buyer accepted the temporary auction suspension but warned that failure of title would trigger return of the deposit or sale of that gear. Han's workers listened from the shed door. Their jobs now sat inside a dispute over public rights without becoming public property themselves. Tian asked whether they could attend the review. Han said yes, then looked as if he regretted answering before arranging what they should say.

canal_p01_068.speaker: narrator
canal_p01_068.text: Bao's hammer disappeared while he spoke with the buyer. He searched the bench, the timber stack and his own belt before a goose emerged from the reeds dragging its leather wrist loop. Han reached for the bird and stepped into mud to his ankle. The goose escaped; the hammer did not. Tian laughed so hard she had to sit on the shed step. Han returned the tool without a speech, then borrowed Luo's bucket to wash his boot beside everyone else's.

canal_p01_069.speaker: narrator
canal_p01_069.text: The clerk posted the first household meeting for the following afternoon. It would hear current uses, completed work and the immediate repair schedule before considering any final charter. Pei Fen offered to bring her old toll notebooks. Bao offered to explain the gate's ordinary condition. Tian offered to help people check their household entries. Yue could assist one preparation while the others proceeded. For once, choosing a useful task did not mean choosing which person she believed was the whole story.

canal_p01_070.speaker: narrator
canal_p01_070.text: Before closing the shed, Luo measured the water against the fixed bank mark. The evening level was lower than the morning's by two thumb-widths, partly because boats had passed and partly because the lower seal leaked. She recorded both known uses and the unresolved loss. Han stood beside her and asked how quickly the new guide could be fitted. The question sounded less like an argument about ownership than anything he had said all day. Luo answered with the actual work date.

canal_p01_071.speaker: narrator
canal_p01_071.text: Yue watched the last grain boat enter the narrow lock under ordinary poles and ropes. Its loaded draft matched the keeper's posted limit. Beyond the north wharf, the spill hollow waited beneath reeds that made it look useless. The eight-week review would need books, dimensions and households able to speak as themselves. Tomorrow's meeting was only the first part. Yue put the measuring stick back on its hooks and chose whom to help prepare.

choices.text: Help Tian prepare the household reading.
Help Pei Fen distinguish her memories and surviving entries.
Help Bao present the gate's physical defect.

canal_p01_072.speaker: narrator
canal_p01_072.text: Tian spread the household list over her sewing table. Yue helped compare each current resident with the old obligation line, leaving space for absent families to answer later. The seamstress kept working between names because a sail was due before dawn. She said a fair meeting should make room for people whose work could not pause merely because a notice declared a convenient hour. They added a second reading at the grain counter, then folded the list away from the lamp.

canal_p01_073.speaker: narrator
canal_p01_073.text: Pei Fen opened a toll notebook with broad columns written before her eyesight weakened. Yue checked its dates against the clerk's calendar copy and helped make a readable extract for tomorrow. The retired clerk wanted to tell everyone what the original annex said. Yue asked her to distinguish memory from the entries they could actually show. Pei grumbled, then wrote 'I remember' above one passage. The phrase preserved her voice without disguising it as a surviving document.

canal_p01_074.speaker: narrator
canal_p01_074.text: Bao placed the worn gate seal beside a straight wooden model. Yue helped label the measured hollow and the binding edge for tomorrow's explanation. The carpenter said villagers sometimes listened better when a broken part sat on the table. He would still need to explain its limits: this seal showed a leak, not who owned the bank. Yue wrote that distinction beneath the diagram. Bao kept it, laughing that a piece of rotten wood was about to become more carefully introduced than he usually was.

canal_p01_075.speaker: narrator
canal_p01_075.text: The keeper's lamp remained lit after the wharf lamps went dark. Yue left the chosen preparation with its owner and returned to her room above the flour store. Her work sheet named twelve paid days across the coming eight weeks, with room for recovery and a return journey. Below it, her private page held the dream canal. She closed that page first. Tomorrow she would hear twenty-eight households whose actual lives could not be lifted or understood all at once.

canal_from_rotation.speaker: narrator
canal_from_rotation.text: Eight days after leaving Salt Lantern Valley, Yue reached the salt-road canal with her ordinary clothes, tablet and food bag. She remembered the valley's measured rotation and Yuan Lian leaving space for tomorrow's correction. The household tokens and working records remained with their keepers. Luo Zhen's invitation described a lock that leaked and an auction notice assigning household labor with the waterway. Yue had brought no solution for that notice. She had brought the habit of checking what a useful number left out.

canal_from_maintenance.speaker: narrator
canal_from_maintenance.text: Eight days after leaving Salt Lantern Valley, Yue reached the salt-road canal with her ordinary clothes, tablet and food bag. She remembered carriers finding the repaired tools and a reserve that gave the valley another interval to decide. Commission equipment remained at its assigned store; the workshop's loan had followed its own return arrangement. Luo Zhen's invitation described a leaking lock and a proposed sale of the waterway. Yue knew maintenance could change people's days. She did not yet know whose days this canal claimed to own.

canal_from_purchase.speaker: narrator
canal_from_purchase.text: Eight days after leaving Salt Lantern Valley, Yue reached the salt-road canal with her ordinary clothes, tablet and food bag. She remembered purchased water actually arriving, and the dirty cover somebody refused before counting it. The source agreement and purchase originals remained in the valley archive. Luo Zhen's invitation described a leaking lock and a sale notice bundling household service with the waterway. Yue had seen a useful purchase made honestly. This proposed purchase would need its own evidence and its own people able to answer.
